# Research and Analysis

Task or skill name given: $ARGUMENTS

1. Pick the one skill below that best fits the task. Take a second only if the task clearly needs both.
2. Read that SKILL.md in full from ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, then follow it.
3. If nothing below fits, carry on without a skill. Never invent a skill name.
4. Tell the user in one line which skill you used.

| Skill file | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `ach-matrix/SKILL.md` | Analysis of Competing Hypotheses in three sizes. Load when the user says "run an ACH", "competing hypotheses", "which hypothesis survives", "score the evidence against each explanation", or "build an ACH matrix". Teaches matrix construction, the CC/C/N/I/II consistency rubric, and ranking by inconsistency so the least-disconfirmed hypothesis wins, never the most-supported. |
| `analytic-tradecraft/SKILL.md` | The reasoning discipline of the Claudify Analyst engine: Structured Analytic Techniques (ACH, Key Assumptions Check, premortem, the named bias sweep), MECE decomposition, the bull/bear/red-team dialectic, and the estimative language standard. Load when framing a research question, scoring evidence against hypotheses, writing or judging a Conviction Dossier, or any time a conclusion is about to be asserted from evidence. This is the skill that stops template-filling from masquerading as analysis. |
| `base-rate-discipline/SKILL.md` | Reference-class forecasting and a growing personal base-rate library. Load when the user says "what's the base rate", "reference class", "outside view first", "how often does this usually succeed", or "what's a sensible prior". The outside view comes before any inside-view story, always. |
| `calibration-drills/SKILL.md` | Probability elicitation and Brier scoring practice for the human who signs the frames. Load when the user says "calibration practice", "am I overconfident", "Brier score", "probability training", or "score my forecasts". The engine keeps its own scoreboard; this is how you build yours. |
| `claudify-analyst/SKILL.md` | The customer-facing product skill for Claudify Analyst: what the buyer gets, how it integrates, how it is positioned and packaged. Load when answering "what is the Analyst tier", writing sales or support copy about it, or onboarding a buyer. Positioning: the specialist research package in the Claudify lineup, designed to compose with the base and the other specialists. |
| `community-evidence-extraction/SKILL.md` | The extraction, audit, repair and grounding-check pipeline for turning a pile of community posts (a forum, a members' community, a newsletter archive, a chat export) into graded evidence cards you can cite. Load when the user says "mine this community", "turn these posts into evidence", "extract case studies", "grade these claims", "audit the cards", or "is this synthesis grounded". Not for live web research on a single question (use /research) and not for a quick summary of one post. |
| `decision-framing/SKILL.md` | Framing a decision so research can serve it: the loss ladder, the signed frame, and the flip condition. Load when the user says "frame this decision", "GO or NO-GO", "what would change my mind", "loss ladder", or "set up the research question properly". Research that cannot name what would change as a result of its answer is entertainment. |
| `due-diligence-checklists/SKILL.md` | Product, market, team, and financial diligence checklists where every item is an observable with a pass/flag criterion. Load when the user says "diligence checklist", "vet this company", "red flags", "verify the claimed numbers", or "should we do this deal". Private output only. |
| `evidence-grading/SKILL.md` | Grading evidence strength from evidence TYPE, never from wording. Load when the user says "how strong is this evidence", "can I trust this number", "grade this source", "likelihood ratio", or "is this claim actually supported". Persuasion words cap credibility, they never raise it. |
| `interval-estimation/SKILL.md` | Quantities are intervals: p10/p50/p90 elicitation and three-scenario reporting. Load when the user says "give me a range not a point", "p10 p50 p90", "how confident is that estimate", "best case worst case", or "this point estimate feels too precise". |
| `market-sizing-methods/SKILL.md` | Top-down, bottom-up, and value-theory market sizing with scope discipline. Load when the user says "size this market", "TAM SAM SOM", "how big is the market", "top-down or bottom-up", or "is this market worth entering". Every size is an interval with a named scope, never a point. |
| `premortem-method/SKILL.md` | The structured premortem: assume the decision failed, write the autopsy, map every line to something checkable. Load when the user says "run a premortem", "why might this fail", "write the autopsy", "what would make this wrong", or "stress test this plan before we commit". |
| `quality-and-calibration/SKILL.md` | The honesty discipline of the Claudify Analyst engine: computed belief, source independence, proper scoring, the anti-gaming guards (G1-G13), and what may never be claimed. Load when assigning likelihood ratios, judging evidence quality, writing or grading predictions, reporting calibration, or any time a number is about to be shown to a human. This is the skill that keeps the scoreboard honest when the scoreboard is ours. |
| `red-team-questioning/SKILL.md` | The red-team question battery: attack the reasoning, never the conclusion. Load when the user says "red team this", "poke holes in this", "challenge my thinking", "what am I missing", or "play devil's advocate properly". Isolation is the mechanism: attack before reading anyone's conclusion. |
| `source-provenance/SKILL.md` | Source liveness, origin tracing, and citation laundering detection. Load when the user says "is this source still live", "who actually said this first", "are these independent sources", "citation laundering", or "check the provenance of this number". N sources tracing to one origin are one vote. |
| `voi-triage/SKILL.md` | Value-of-information triage: research what can change the decision, skip what cannot. Load when the user says "what should I research next", "is this worth researching", "value of information", "when do we stop researching", or "where does the research budget go". |
